source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check the information of test item

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: Information should be correct and still be correct after rebooting

original_test_intent: Verify the SMBIOS Type 0 Vendor string equals the platform-approved BIOS vendor and remains identical after reboot, while retaining the complete Type 0 context needed to detect malformed or mismatched identity data.
original_method: Collect raw dmidecode Type 0 plus the bios-vendor string on the mapped SUT, compare with the approved exact vendor, execute the approved reboot plan, repeat collection and compare the same field and surrounding record.
manual_activity: One authorized user may approve the unchanged plan and expected vendor. The Vendor collection, comparison, reboot and post-check can then be software-controlled.
required_inputs: Exact BIOS Vendor string and allowed normalization
safety_requirements: Archive complete raw Type 0 output before extracting Vendor.
Do not accept any non-empty string; compare the exact approved value and platform mapping.
Run reboot only under the approved plan with OOB recovery and stop on boot/management loss or identity drift.
agent_execution_scope: Collect dmidecode/tool/platform evidence, compare exact Vendor before/after the approved reboot and flag drift/anomalies.
Do not change SMBIOS/firmware, invent expected strings or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve expected Vendor, normalization, reboot and recovery.
Review mismatches and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: sudo dmidecode -t 0 is appropriate and full output is valuable; sshpass and disabled host-key validation are not acceptable default assumptions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use approved authenticated transport; archive dmidecode --version, full -t 0 output and -s bios-vendor before and after reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The linked script, Type 0 Vendor scope and 5/5-minute fields are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: EXACT VENDOR WITH RAW TYPE 0 CONTEXT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind exact Vendor comparison to board/BIOS identity, retain raw Type 0 and tool version, and run the same deterministic check before/after the approved reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record dmidecode, SMBIOS, BIOS and kernel versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Installed dmidecode documentation and platform SMBIOS recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact expectation, provenance and deterministic persistence evidence without replacing dmidecode.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; focuses acceptance on Vendor while retaining the whole record.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Whitespace/case normalization must be explicitly approved; raw bytes/text remain authoritative.

project_override_considerations: A project may define its platform-specific Vendor string or normalization. The override must be recorded and cannot modify the master source.
expected_evidence: Approval, expected Vendor, platform/firmware identity and dmidecode version
Raw pre-reboot Type 0 and vendor summary
Raw post-reboot output and exact Vendor diff

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Item, generic procedure and persistence criteria consistently identify a read-only Type 0 Vendor check.
